title: Privilege Journey Mapping and Evidence Batching Strategy
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a proposed mapping exercise we call the "Privilege Journey" and an associated evidence batching strategy for quarterly least-privilege recertification and privileged access audits. Goal: make access reviews fast, reproducible, and SIEM-friendly so evidence exports are automatable and reviewers can focus on decisions rather than data collection.

Scope:
- Applies to cloud IAM roles, RBAC v2 role definitions, service accounts, and on-prem privileged accounts tracked in the entitlement catalog.
- Includes audit log schema fields, SIEM export patterns (ELK/Splunk), and evidence batching conventions for quarterly recertification and ad-hoc privileged audits.
- Excludes fine-grained application-level permissions tied only to product feature flags (these are handled by product teams; we will provide templates).

Background & Motivation:
We repeatedly hit two friction points during recertification: 1) reviewers lack a concise, unified view of "why" someone has a privilege (approval path, last use, owner), and 2) evidence requests require manual artifact gathering (playbooks, approvals, login traces). RBAC v2 gives us richer role metadata; we need a consistent mapping from role metadata -> reviewer view + SIEM evidence export to support automation.

Definitions (for this doc):
- Privilege Journey: the lifecycle trail for any entitlement from grant -> use -> review -> revoke or retain.
- Evidence Batch: a single tarball / archive of artifacts for one entitlement-review pair (naming schema below).
- Reviewer Snapshot: condensed JSON/markdown that summarizes an entitlement for the reviewer UI.

Privilege Journey Mapping (high level):
1) Entitlement metadata (RBAC v2): role_id, role_description, grant_type (manual/automated), grantor, grantee, grant_date, expiry (optional), tier (privileged/standard), ownership (team/service), linked_jira_prs, linked_incidents.
2) Last-use signals: last API call with token (timestamp), last console/ssh event, last GitOps commit that required the role.
3) Approval trail: approver_id(s), approval_date(s), approval_ticket (Jira/Confluence id), justification text.
4) Compensating controls: MFA_required, IP_restrictions, session_duration_limit, just_in_time_flag.
5) Evidence artifacts: approval PDFs, screenshots of ticket, SIEM export slice, session logs, change-control PRs.

Reviewer Snapshot (single-file output):
- Human title: <role_id> - <grantee_name> (<team>)
- One-line summary: why they have it (from approval justification)
- Grant path: [grantor] -> [approval_ticket] -> [date]
- Last use: ISO timestamp + verb (api/console/ssh)
- Controls: enumerated
- Risk score: heuristic (see scoring below)
- Link to Evidence Batch (S3/GS URI)

Evidence Batching Strategy (what to include and why):
- Naming convention: evidence_<role_id>_<grantee>_<quarter>_<YYYYMMDD>.tar.gz
- Minimum batch contents:
  - snapshot.md (the Reviewer Snapshot)
  - approvals.pdf (export of Jira/Confluence approval) or approval.txt
  - use_events.json (SIEM slice; see schema below)
  - control_checks.txt (MFA/IP/JIT check results)
  - owner_response.txt (if owner provided comments during review)
  - manifest.sha256
- Retention: keep batch in secure bucket for 3 years (audit requirement) then archive to cold storage.

SIEM Export / Audit Log Schema (recommended minimal fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- principal_type (user|service_account|role)
- principal_id
- action (assume-role|generate-token|console-login|ssh|api-call)
- resource_type (project|vm|bucket|dataset|repo)
- resource_id
- source_ip
- user_agent
- outcome (success|failure)
- session_id (if available)
- request_id / trace_id
- additional_metadata (stringified kv pairs or links to traced logs)
Notes: produce SIEM slices filtered to principal_id + window [grant_date - 1d, now] (or 90 days if grant_date is older than 90d). Keep CSV and ndjson exports.

Sample Splunk/KQL/Elastic queries (templates):
- Splunk (last 90d, principal_id): index=audit (principal_id="{{PRINCIPAL}}") | where timestamp >= "{{START}}" | table timestamp action resource_type resource_id source_ip outcome
- KQL (Azure Sentinel): AuditLogs | where PrincipalId == "{{PRINCIPAL}}" and TimeGenerated >= datetime({{START}}) | project TimeGenerated, OperationName, ResultDescription, IPAddress
- Elastic (ndjson example): POST _search {
  "query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"principal_id": "{{PRINCIPAL}}"}}, {"range": {"timestamp": {"gte": "{{START}}"}}}]}}}

Risk Scoring Heuristic (simple, reviewer-friendly):
- Base score by tier: privileged=50, standard=10
- Add +20 if no recent use in 90d and expiry == null
- Add +15 if grant path lacks >=1 approver with SSO-bound identity
- Subtract -10 if compensating controls strong (MFA + IP whitelist + JIT enabled)
- Final clamped 0-100; color bands: 0-29 green, 30-59 amber, 60-100 red

Automation Implementation Plan (short):
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): export current RBAC v2 role metadata and build snapshot.md generator (lambda job) that emits Reviewer Snapshot and writes to staging bucket. Ticket: SAC-4123.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): SIEM slice generator jobs (per SIEM backend) that produce use_events.json and push to evidence bucket; integrate manifest.sha256.
- Phase 3 (3 weeks): UI flow for reviewers to fetch Evidence Batch links; attach to recertification workflow.
- Phase 4 (ongoing): schedule cron for quarterly batch generation; add delta-only incremental batches for mid-quarter privileged audits.

Operational Details & Playbooks (practical):
- On-demand audit: reviewer requests evidence via Jira form -> automation job queued -> evidence batch produced within SLA (30m for privileged, 2h for standard).
- Revocation flow: if reviewer marks "revoke" then automate ticket creation in access-control queue with pre-filled justification and owners notified.
- Emergency access: evidence batch should include temporary-grant justification and time-bounded session logs.

Checklist for Quarterly Recertification (for each entitlement):
- [ ] Reviewer Snapshot exists and is < 1 page
- [ ] Evidence Batch present and validated (manifest.sha256 match)
- [ ] Risk score computed
- [ ] Owner comment captured
- [ ] Decision logged (retain/revoke/conditional) with action owner and ETA

Storage & Access Controls for Evidence Batches:
- Store in encrypted bucket (KMS-managed keys). Access to batches limited to security-reviewer role and audit-operators.
- Access logs forwarded to SIEM (ingest events describing who downloaded evidence).

Open Questions / To resolve:
- Should we include full trace/span dumps for high-risk entitlements (cost and privacy considerations)? ACTION: engineering to estimate export size for top-200 privileged principals.
- Columnar vs ndjson exports for SIEM: which gives best downstream analytics for security telemetry?
- How to surface owner responses when owner is an external contractor with limited SSO identity?

Notes to self (raw):
- Prioritize small, review-friendly snapshot. Too much data = reviewer fatigue.
- Talk to observability about retaining raw session logs for 90d as minimum.
- Talk to legal on retention beyond 3y.

References and links (quick):
- RBAC v2 design notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SAC/RBAC+v2+Design+Notes
- SIEM export format proposal (doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SAC/SIEM+export+proposal
- SAC-4123: Evidence batching PoC (Jira)

Next steps (short-term):
- Run pilot for 10 high-risk entitlements this quarter: generate batches, invite 3 reviewers, collect feedback.
- Engineering: estimate S3 cost and pipeline time for full-company quarterly run.

If you are reviewing: please comment inline or add to SAC-4123.
